Which of the following is the primary function of a commercial bank?
B) Accept deposits and provide loans
The primary functions of a commercial bank are accepting deposits and providing loans/advances.
The process of converting black money into white money through banking channels is called
Money laundering is the process of making illegally-gained proceeds appear legal.
Which of the following is NOT a type of bank account?
Mutual Fund is an investment product, not a bank account type.
The 'Banking Ombudsman Scheme' was introduced by RBI in
The Banking Ombudsman Scheme was introduced in 1995.
Which of the following is a 'Scheduled Bank'?
A) All banks registered with RBI
B) Banks included in the Second Schedule of RBI Act
Scheduled banks are those included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934.
The 'Dual Control' system in banking refers to
A) Two managers for one branch
B) Regulation by both RBI and State Government
Dual control means banking regulation is shared between RBI (for banking aspects) and State Government (for cooperative aspects).
Which of the following is the 'Lender of Last Resort'?
RBI acts as the Lender of Last Resort, providing emergency liquidity to banks.

Which of the following is a 'Universal Bank'?
A) Bank providing only savings accounts
B) Bank providing all types of financial services
D) Bank providing only foreign exchange
A universal bank provides a wide range of financial services including banking, insurance, investment, etc.
The 'Banking Regulation Act' was enacted in
The Banking Regulation Act was enacted in 1949.
Which of the following is NOT a principle of banking?
The three principles of banking are Safety, Liquidity and Profitability. Risk-taking is not a principle.
The 'Cash Reserve Ratio' (CRR) is maintained by banks with
CRR is the percentage of deposits that banks must maintain with RBI.
Which of the following is a 'Cooperative Bank'?
Saraswat Cooperative Bank is a cooperative bank.
The 'Non-Banking Financial Company' (NBFC) is regulated by
NBFCs are regulated by RBI under the RBI Act, 1934.
Which of the following is a 'Payment Bank'?
Airtel Payments Bank is a payment bank.
The 'Small Finance Bank' license requires minimum capital of
Small Finance Banks require minimum capital of ₹100 crore.
Which of the following is the 'Banker to Banks'?
RBI is the banker to all banks.

DICGC insures bank deposits up to ₹5 lakh per depositor.
Which of the following is a 'Foreign Bank' operating in India?
Citibank is a foreign bank operating in India.
The 'Priority Sector Lending' (PSL) target for domestic banks is
Domestic banks must lend 40% of their adjusted net bank credit to priority sectors.
Which of the following is a 'Regional Rural Bank' (RRB)?
Prathama Bank is a Regional Rural Bank.

The Lead Bank Scheme was introduced in 1969.
Which of the following is a 'Local Area Bank'?
Coastal Local Area Bank is a Local Area Bank.
